thread:
anya: quick question — we need to finalize TTL + access-priority for traces before the console rollout. current draft: prod hot=30d, prod-cold=365d, staging=14d, dev=3d. rehydrate SLA target = 2h for prod, 12h for staging. thoughts on routing/quotas and billing impact?
jonathan: 30d hot seems fine, but 365d cold will blow storage costs for tenant-heavy clusters. can we do auto-compact after 90d and keep only sampled spans? :thinking_face:
liam: agree with jonathan. proposal: cold tier = 180d with compacting to 1% sample after 90d, and a cheaper object-store-only export. rehydrate SLA needs to be opt-in per tenant (paid).
maria: +1 on opt-in paid rehydrate. also we need a clear console affordance: toggle rehydrate for a tenant, estimated cost preview, and estimated time window. engineers shouldn't have to file tickets.
anya: yes console UX must show cost delta. also, can we route queries by access priority tag? e.g., queries with header X-Redwood-Priority=high hit hot replicas and bypass cold fetch. default for support/alerts = high.
liam: we already have routing policy code but not priority header enforcement. would be a ~1 day task to plug into query router. the bigger work is quota enforcement to avoid abuse.
samira: on quotas — suggest we add a separate rehydrate budget per tenant. free tier gets 1 rehydrate/month, paid tiers get more. that prevents accidental runaway costs.
jonathan: what about developer sandboxes? dev traces should rarely rehydrate. maybe keep dev low retention (3d) and no rehydrate unless explicitly enabled by owner.
maria: agree. also add audit trail: who triggered rehydrate and cost charged. P0 for compliance.
anya: rough config snippet I sketched for ops to review:
```
trace_ttl:
  prod:
    hot_days: 30
    cold_days: 180
    compact_after_days: 90
    rehydrate_sla_hours: 2
  staging:
    hot_days: 14
    cold_days: 90
    compact_after_days: 30
    rehydrate_sla_hours: 12
  dev:
    hot_days: 3
    cold_days: 7
    compact_after_days: 3
    rehydrate_sla_hours: 72
routing:
  priority_header: X-Redwood-Priority
  hot_threshold: high
rebilling:
  rehydrate_paid: true
  free_tier_rehydrates_per_month: 1
```
liam: that looks good as a starting point. edge-case: what if a tenant queries older traces frequently? should we cache rehydrated results for short window and meter by tokens/queries?
anya: yep plan to cache rehydrated chunks for 24h and meter by query-units. console will show per-tenant estimated cost.
jonathan: ops question — if compacted spans keep only sampled traces, rehydrate cannot restore full fidelity. need clear docs/UI note. also add a fallback: if full-fidelity needed, trigger on-demand full restore to longer-term archive (longer SLA + higher cost).
maria: docs + in-console warning is good. UX: show 'full fidelity restore will incur $X and take ~Y hours' with confirm modal.
infra-bot: Deploy notice: feature/trace-ttl-config pushed to staging cluster at 1932107000, migration job scheduled.
samira: note for SREs — migration will rewrite indexes; expect increased I/O for ~2 hours. scheduled window 02:00-04:00 UTC.
liam: can we add a soft-limit to block full-restore requests when migration I/O > threshold? to avoid cascading load.
anya: yes add a circuit-breaker in router that checks cluster-load-metrics before allowing rehydrate requests. fallback to queue with ETA.
jonathan: final ask — we need telemetry: per-tenant rehydrate counts, cost charged, average restore duration, failure rate. tie to billing events.
maria: I'll add dashboard tiles: rehydrate QPS, average SLA, cost per restore, top 10 tenants by restore spend.
anya: awesome. let's iterate on the config and console mockups. next sync: quick async review in the doc, then 30m design check tomorrow. :thumbsup:
